chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A people will come after you, and the one man among them will have the reward of fifty of you.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we were with you at Badr, Uhud, and Hunain, and the Quran was revealed among us.' He said: 'Indeed, if you were to bear what they bore, you would not be as patient as they are.'

key_terms.أُحُد: The Battle of Uhud, a major battle where the Prophet was wounded
key_terms.بَدْر: The Battle of Badr, a pivotal early battle in Islam
key_terms.حُنَيْن: The Battle of Hunayn, a significant victory after the conquest of Mecca
key_terms.صَبْر: Patience and perseverance in the face of trials

ai.seo_question: Why does the Prophet say one person from the future will equal fifty companions in reward?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this hadith to highlight the unique spiritual station of the followers of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) during the period of the Great Occultation. The Prophet’s response clarifies that while the Companions’ merit was rooted in immediate presence and revelation, the future believers’ reward stems from their steadfast endurance of prolonged trials and solitude in faith. This distinction underscores the Shia view that the trials of the Ghayba require a different, yet equally profound, form of patience (sabr) that merits superior recompense.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 467 - It is narrated from Hasan bin Mahbub from Abdullah bin Sinan from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) said: “Very soon will come a people after you, each of whom will be eligible for fifty times your reward. They said: O Messenger of Allah (s), we lived in your company, fought the Badr, Uhad and Hunain battles with you and the Holy Quran came down among us? The Prophet said: Indeed, if you were to face what they faced, you will not be as patient as them.”
